newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks close 7.87 pct up on baht flotation.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks close 7.87 pct up on baht flotation.

text.p: Thai stocks soared to end 7.87 percent higher in active trade on Wednesday as foreign investors bought large capitalised stocks folowing a decision by the Thai government to float the baht, brokers said.
The composite SET index rose 41.51 points to 568.79 on 10.4 billion baht turnover. The SET-50 index advanced 3.54 points to 41.74.

"Foreigners today bought blue-chip stocks with high liquidity, especially banking, finance, communication and energy issues. They believe the worst is over for the Thai baht following the announcement on baht flotation by the central bank," said Bumnan Liumsuwan of Asia Credit.
The Bank of Thailand and the ministry of finance early on Wednesday announced that the Thai exchange rate system would be changed to a managed float, effective immediately.
Brokers said investors reacted positively to what they said was a de-facto devaluation of the baht.
